name: The Sierra Club Foundation: lands, clean air and outdoors (charityevals)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: EPA's soot standard and the outdoors trips reach people in the United States.
summary: The Sierra Club Foundation's grants to the Sierra Club for public lands and waters, clean air and water and the outdoors programmes (its Our Wild America lands campaign and, by our judgment, half its other grants outside Beyond Coal; $35.2M in 2024) are modelled from what can be put on the site's scale in 2022-2024: the Sierra Club's share of EPA's 2024 fine-particle (soot) standard (about {{row:pm_deaths_per_year}} deaths a year avoided once in effect; upheld in court in 2026) and the 5,127 people a year on its Inspiring Connections Outdoors trips. At the defaults it gives about {{result}} years of healthy life per $1,000 after the standard's compliance costs (EPA's own figure), nearly all from the soot standard; it is low because the Sierra Club is one of many groups behind the rule (4%), advocacy is credited with only part of it, the deaths are mostly of older adults and come years later, and the lands wins (monuments, the Public Lands Rule, Western Arctic leasing limits, mostly rescinded in 2025) count only in a share for other work, since their species and unleased oil and gas don't reach the scale. The biggest uncertainties are the share of the rule due to advocacy, the next dollar and how much of the rule is delivered; both branches are discounted for missing data.

sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for outcomes in more than one unit (docs/normalization.md 2.6): each outcome is counted in its own unit (units of value for income and deaths, WELLBYs for life satisfaction, tonnes of CO₂e, chicken pain days) and put into this model's unit by its unit's conversion over this unit's, which the headline's conversion cancels. So each moves only with its own sliders, exactly as in a model of its own unit. The rows are fixed; don't edit them.

rows.label: Cost of a typical year of 2022-2024, in 2024 dollars
Hectares protected (none counted here)
rows.explainer: No land is counted in hectares: the Sierra Club's lands wins of the period (national monuments added or enlarged, among them two historic sites in 2024; the Bureau of Land Management's Public Lands Rule and its bonding and royalty rule; the Western Arctic's 13 million acres closed to new leasing; the Thompson Divide's 200,000 acres of forest withdrawn from new oil, gas and mining leases for 20 years) protect land mostly from drilling, mining and roads rather than forest from clearing, so the template's per-hectare land carbon doesn't apply. Their good is fossil carbon left unleased, counted in the other work's share (unmodelled_benefits_adj), since the Public Lands Rule and the Western Arctic rule were rescinded in 2025 and the Thompson Divide withdrawal, which stands, covers land with few expected new wells.

rows.label: EPA soot standard (2024): deaths a year avoided once in effect
rows.explainer: The shared figure for this rule (facts: climate): {{row:pm_deaths_per_year}} a year (1,900 to 5,700), between the two estimates of EPA's regulatory impact analysis for 2032, 4,500 for all adults and 2,100 for the over-64s.

rows.label: Inspiring Connections Outdoors: participants a year

source.title: Sierra Club, Form 990 for 2024 (IRS e-file XML, object 202503169349309600), Schedule O, Part III line 4a
source.quote: THE INSPIRING CONNECTIONS OUTDOORS (ICO) PROGRAM, FOR EXAMPLE, RAN 254 TRIPS FOR 5,127 YOUTH AND ADULTS

rows.explainer: Youth and adults on the Sierra Club's Inspiring Connections Outdoors trips in 2024 (254 trips), mostly from under-served communities, led by volunteers and funded from the Foundation's charitable grants. The chapters' and groups' other outings ('tens of thousands' of participants) are left out: they are mostly members' own hikes and trips, who would spend time outdoors anyway, so their gain over what they'd have done is small and unmeasured; they are in the other work's share.

rows.label: People whose health is counted directly in DALYs (none: deaths and IQ are valued in units of value)
People whose life satisfaction gains from protected nature (not counted)
rows.explainer: Not counted: no study links a protected monument or withdrawal to measured life satisfaction of its visitors or neighbours; the outdoors trips are a branch of their own (out_).

rows.label: Livelihoods: people whose income the work changes (none counted)
rows.explainer: None counted: the lands wins keep land open to its current users (ranchers, hunters, tribes, visitors) rather than changing their incomes, and no study measures an income change from them.

rows.label: Wild animal-years changed (not counted)
rows.explainer: The species wins (grizzly bears' and wolves' protections kept in court, salmon on the Snake River) leave more wild animals alive; whether a wild animal's life is better or worse than none is unknown, so their welfare is left out (0).

rows.label: Share of each won rule due to advocacy at all (all groups together)
rows.explainer: The shared figure for a won policy (facts: climate.advocacy_share_of_policy_win, {{row:p_success}}, 10% to 60%), whose reference class is policy in general, so it serves the soot standard too. The Foundation's part of the advocates' work is the branch's attribution row.

rows.label: Years a won rule counts before it would have come anyway
Years from a won rule until its effects come (shared wait; no branch here uses it)
rows.explainer: The shared wait for rules (3 years, 1 to 6), kept for the template's protection_years row; the soot standard has its own wait (pm_wait) and no land or tonnes are counted.

rows.label: Discounted years of impact after the shared wait (no branch here uses it)
Tonnes of CO₂e per hectare a year (no land counted)
Value of a heart or lung death at 70 or older (units of value)
rows.explainer: GiveWell's five-year weights for 70-74 and 75-79 (their mean) and for 80 and over, mixed by the share of US cardiovascular deaths at 70 or older that are at 80 or older (families/high-income-care.md).

rows.label: Value of an adult heart or lung death averted in the US (units of value)
rows.explainer: The ages of US cardiovascular deaths (facts: death_ages, GBD 2023: 74% at 70 or older) valued by GiveWell's weights by age, × the value-of-a-life slider: EPA's soot deaths are mostly heart and lung deaths of older adults.

rows.label: EPA soot standard: value of a death averted
rows.explainer: The US value of a heart or lung death (row above).

rows.label: EPA soot standard: years lived with illness averted per death averted
rows.explainer: Illness comes with the deaths (heart attacks, strokes, lung disease): the shared share of a rich country's cardiovascular DALYs that is illness (cvd_yld_share_gbr, 14%) over its deaths per DALY (cvd_deaths_per_daly_gbr), so both describe one population; the UK stands in for the US, the nearest the facts hold. About {{row:pm_illness_dalys_per_death}} healthy years of illness per death, counted in healthy years (row pm_illness_dalys).

rows.label: EPA soot standard: years from the win (2024) until the deaths are avoided
rows.explainer: The shared figure for this rule (facts: climate): 9 years from 2024 (7 to 11); EPA assumed attainment in late 2032 after designations in late 2025, and designations are now due by February 2027.

rows.label: EPA soot standard: discounted years of impact
EPA soot standard: expected units of value from deaths, before adjustments
EPA soot standard: expected illness averted before adjustments (DALYs)
Inspiring Connections Outdoors: life satisfaction gained per participant a year (WELLBYs)

source.title: White et al. (2019), Spending at least 120 minutes a week in nature is associated with good health and wellbeing, Scientific Reports 9, 7730
source.quote: spending at least 120 mins a week in nature is associated with good health and wellbeing

rows.explainer: A participant takes one or a few day trips a year. Anchor: White et al.'s 19,806 English adults report higher life satisfaction when they spend two hours a week in nature, a cross-sectional association; a trip's effect on a 0-10 life-satisfaction scale is a few tenths of a point for some days, perhaps more for a youth who returns to nature. Our judgment, 0.005 WELLBYs a participant (0.001 to 0.03, the top for a lasting habit), net of what the day would have held otherwise.

rows.label: Inspiring Connections Outdoors: WELLBYs over the period, before adjustments
rows.explainer: A yearly service, counted for each year of the period (the model divides by the period's years), with no win years or waits.

rows.label: Healthy years per person-year counted directly (none)
Life-satisfaction gain per person-year (not counted)
Livelihoods: ln(consumption) gain per person per year (none counted)
Pain days per wild animal-year changed (not counted)
Deaths in a catastrophe the work lowers (none counted)
rows.explainer: The Foundation's lands, clean-air and outdoors work isn't credited with lowering a global catastrophe's chance.

rows.label: Cut in a catastrophe's yearly chance (none counted)
Value of a death in a catastrophe (none counted; the shared value of an older adult's death)
rows.explainer: Unused here (no catastrophe counted); kept so the template's rows stay whole.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment: how far the regulators' estimates and the judged reach should be trusted
rows.explainer: Used by the outdoors branch: the wellbeing gain of a trip rests on cross-sectional and short-term studies of time in nature, not a trial of these trips. Our judgment, 0.8 (0.5 to 1.1); the soot standard reads the rule's shared evidence row.

rows.label: EPA soot standard: evidence adjustment on EPA's deaths
rows.explainer: The shared figure for this rule (facts: climate): 1 (0.7 to 1.2); the doubt about EPA's two estimates is already in the shared deaths figure.

rows.label: EPA soot standard: share of the deaths that wouldn't have been avoided anyway
rows.explainer: The shared figure for this rule (facts: climate): {{row:pm_counterfactual_adj}} (70% to 100%); EPA's baseline already holds the rules then in force.

rows.label: EPA soot standard: the Sierra Club's share of the advocacy behind the win
rows.explainer: The Sierra Club's members and chapters pressed EPA for a stricter fine-particle standard in the 2023 hearings and comments, and it is among the groups that intervened to defend the standard in the D.C. Circuit (upheld 26 June 2026); its lawyers' part is small, since Earthjustice was the intervenors' counsel. Others: the Environmental Defense Fund, the American Lung Association, NRDC, the Clean Air Task Force and community groups. Our judgment, 4% (2% to 10%) for the Sierra Club's own comments, hearings and members only.

source.title: Kentucky v. EPA (D.C. Cir. No. 24-1050), unopposed motion of health and environmental groups to intervene in support of EPA, 27 March 2024
source.note: The Sierra Club is among the intervenors, with Earthjustice as their counsel.

rows.label: The Foundation's share of the Sierra Club's resources behind these wins
rows.explainer: The shared figure for both Foundation models (facts: sierra_club_foundation.share_of_sierra_club_resources, {{row:scf_share}}, 50% to 90%): the Foundation funds the Sierra Club's charitable campaigns; the Sierra Club's own money is among the others' resources.

rows.label: EPA soot standard: the Foundation's share of the advocacy resources behind the win
rows.explainer: The Sierra Club's share × the Foundation's part of the Sierra Club's resources.

rows.label: This charity's share of the good done with money, work or budgets it brings in
rows.explainer: The site's one setting for resources another party commits only because of the organisation (docs/normalization.md 2.24): governments' budgets and enforcement, companies' compliance, the use others make of research. The charity is credited this share of the good done with them, net of their cost; the rest stays with those who paid or did the work. Fixed.

rows.label: EPA soot standard: share of credit used
EPA soot standard: share of the win's deaths avoided
rows.explainer: The shared figure for this rule (facts: climate): 50% (20% to 80%); upheld in June 2026, but EPA means to reconsider it, states have gone to the Supreme Court and designations are late.

rows.label: Counted less where the outcome isn't measured for this charity
rows.explainer: Both branches: no death or life-satisfaction gain is measured for the Sierra Club's work (Convention 12).

rows.label: EPA soot standard: all adjustments combined
Inspiring Connections Outdoors: paid resources' share of all the resources behind the trips (volunteers' time valued at the US wage)
rows.explainer: 254 trips a year, each with two to four volunteer leaders for a day or a weekend plus planning, about 10,000 to 25,000 volunteer hours, worth $0.3M to $0.8M at a US wage of about $30 an hour, beside the staff, transport and gear the Sierra Club pays for (the programme's paid cost is not reported apart; similar to the volunteer time, judged). Our judgment, 50% (30% to 70%).

rows.label: Inspiring Connections Outdoors: the Foundation's share of the resources behind the trips
rows.explainer: The trips are led by unpaid volunteers with the Sierra Club's staff and the Foundation's grants: the Foundation's part of the Sierra Club's resources (scf_share) × the paid share of all the resources behind the trips, the volunteers' time valued at the local wage counted as others' resources (templates.md Convention 2).

rows.label: Inspiring Connections Outdoors: all adjustments combined
rows.explainer: The judged gain is already net of what participants would have done instead, so no separate counterfactual; every participant counted took a trip.

rows.label: EPA soot standard: adjustments applied
Inspiring Connections Outdoors: credit used
Leverage and funging (none counted)
rows.explainer: No separate step: others' resources are in each branch's attribution row.

rows.label: EPA soot standard: deaths, in healthy years, before adjustments
EPA soot standard: healthy years before adjustments (weight for the averages)
Inspiring Connections Outdoors: healthy years before adjustments
Share of the outcome that wouldn't have happened anyway (outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only)
The Foundation's share of the resources behind the outcome (outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only)
rows.formula: (pm_dalys_raw * pm_counterfactual_adj * pm_attribution_share_shared + out_dalys_raw * out_attribution_share) / (pm_dalys_raw * pm_counterfactual_adj + out_dalys_raw)

rows.label: Share of credit used (outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only)
Share delivered (outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only)
rows.formula: (pm_dalys_raw * pm_counterfactual_adj * pm_attribution_share * pm_implementation_adj + out_dalys_raw * out_attribution_share) / (pm_dalys_raw * pm_counterfactual_adj * pm_attribution_share + out_dalys_raw * out_attribution_share)

rows.label: All adjustments combined (outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only)
Other work of the period not modelled, as a share of the modelled value
rows.explainer: Left out of the branches, which cover only a small part of this model's cost (the clean-air work behind the soot standard and the outdoors trips): the lands wins (Our Wild America, $17.2M and $15.0M in 2022 and 2023; national monuments; the Public Lands Rule, the bonding and royalty rule and the Western Arctic leasing rule, the first and last rescinded in 2025; the Thompson Divide withdrawal, which stands), the Snake River salmon commitments, the defence of grizzly and wolf protections, the EXPLORE Act and park and urban-tree grants, clean-water and toxic-air cases (the 2023 closing of the startup-shutdown-malfunction loophole), and the chapters' local work. Their spending is in the cost, so leaving them out would count them as worth nothing. On this scale they are worth far less a dollar than the soot work: their species count nothing here, and their good is fossil fuel left unleased, of which a large part, around half in supply-side studies of US federal leasing (Erickson & Lazarus 2018; Prest 2022), is produced elsewhere instead, on mostly rescinded rules. Our judgment, 30% of the modelled value (10% to 80%): the unmodelled work is most of the cost, at perhaps a twentieth of the soot work's value per dollar.

source.title: Sierra Club, Form 990 for 2024 (IRS e-file XML, object 202503169349309600), Schedule O, Part III line 4a
source.quote: WE SECURED THE ENACTMENT OF THE PUBLIC LANDS RULE, WHICH REQUIRES FEDERAL LAND MANAGERS TO PUT CONSERVATION ON A LEVEL PLAYING FIELD WITH MINING AND DRILLING.

rows.label: Deaths and income, in units of value, after adjustments
rows.formula: pm_uov * pm_credit + livelihood_people * ln_gain_per_person_year * protection_years * $uov_per_ln_consumption + catastrophe_deaths * annual_risk_reduction * protection_years * catastrophe_value_per_death + (pm_compliance_uov) / (1 + unmodelled_benefits_adj)
rows.explainer: The won rules' compliance costs (docs/normalization.md 2.21, negative) are added here, divided by one plus the unmodelled-benefits share so that share, applied to the total below, doesn't scale them.

rows.label: Livelihoods and catastrophic risk, in healthy years
PM2.5 standard: compliance costs, units of value (negative)
rows.formula: -@compliance_costs.us_pm_naaqs_2024_cost_per_year * @cpi.usa_2024 / @cpi.usa_2017 * $uov_per_ln_consumption / (@public_funds.compliance_cost_payer_multiple * @united_states.ce_expenditure_per_person_2024) * p_success * pm_years * pm_counterfactual_adj * pm_attribution_share * pm_implementation_adj * missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The won rule's compliance costs (docs/normalization.md 2.21): control costs in 2032 (EPA's regulatory impact analysis, $590 million a year), in 2017 dollars moved to 2024's, valued as money lost by those who bear it, consumers and owners (@public_funds.compliance_cost_payer_multiple, 1.2 times average US consumption), on the log scale; over the same years and wait as the rule's benefits, with the branch's chance, counterfactual, credit, delivered share and missing-data step, not its evidence adjustment (which is about the benefits).

rows.formula: tco2e_bridged * (($deaths_per_tco2e * $climate_heat_share * ((1 - methane_share) * (1 + $discount_rate) ^ -$climate_heat_death_delay + methane_share * @climate.methane_heat_deaths_vs_co2 * (1 + $discount_rate) ^ -@climate.methane_heat_death_delay) * (1 + $side_effect_weight * @climate.nondeath_damages_vs_deaths) * (@death_ages.heat_share_under5 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_under5 + @death_ages.heat_share_5_14 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_5_14 + @death_ages.heat_share_15_49 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_15_49 + @death_ages.heat_share_50plus * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_50_74) + ($deaths_per_tco2e * (1 - $climate_heat_share) * air_pollution_weight + extra_deaths_per_tco2e + methane_share * @climate.ozone_deaths_per_tco2e_methane / (1 + ln(1 + $discount_rate) * @climate.methane_lifetime_years)) * (@death_ages.air_pollution_share_under5 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_under5 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_5_14 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_5_14 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_15_49 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_15_49 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_50plus * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_50_74)) * $life_value_multiplier) / ($uov_per_daly)
